{{Short description|Type of geometric quantity}}
{{about-distinguish-text|the spacetime concept|the independent variable in [[Spectral estimation|spectral analysis]]}}

The '''spectral dimension''' is a [[real number|real-valued]] quantity that characterizes a [[spacetime]] [[geometry]] and [[topology]]. It characterizes a spread into space over time, e.g. an ink drop [[diffusing]] in a water glass or the evolution of a [[pandemic]] in a population. Its definition is as follow: if a phenomenon spreads as <math>t^n</math>, with <math>t</math> the time, then the spectral dimension is <math>2n</math>. The spectral dimension depends on the topology of the space, e.g., the distribution of neighbors in a population, and the diffusion rate. 

In [[physics]], the concept of spectral dimension is used, among other things, in 
[[quantum gravity]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ambjørn | first1=J. | last2=Jurkiewicz | first2=J. | last3=Loll | first3=R. | title=The Spectral Dimension of the Universe is Scale Dependent | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=95 | issue=17 | date=2005-10-20 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.95.171301 | article-number=171301| pmid=16383815 | arxiv=hep-th/0505113 | bibcode=2005PhRvL..95q1301A | s2cid=15496735 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Modesto | first=Leonardo | title=Fractal spacetime from the area spectrum | journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity | volume=26 | issue=24 | date=2009-11-24 | issn=0264-9381 | doi=10.1088/0264-9381/26/24/242002 | article-number=242002|arxiv=0812.2214| s2cid=118826379 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hořava | first=Petr | title=Spectral Dimension of the Universe in Quantum Gravity at a Lifshitz Point | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=102 | issue=16 | date=2009-04-20 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.102.161301 | article-number=161301| pmid=19518693 |arxiv=0902.3657| bibcode=2009PhRvL.102p1301H | s2cid=8799552 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Lauscher|first=Oliver|author2=Reuter, Martin|title=Ultraviolet fixed point and generalized flow equation of quantum gravity|journal=Physical Review D|year=2001|volume=65|issue=2|article-number=025013|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.65.025013|arxiv=hep-th/0108040|bibcode = 2001PhRvD..65b5013L |s2cid=1926982}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Lauscher|first=Oliver|author2=Reuter, Martin|title=Fractal spacetime structure in asymptotically safe gravity|journal=Journal of High Energy Physics|year=2005|volume=2005|issue=10|page=050|doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2005/10/050|arxiv=hep-th/0508202|bibcode = 2005JHEP...10..050L |s2cid=14396108}}</ref> 
[[Percolation critical exponents|percolation theory]], 
[[superstring theory]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Atick | first1=Joseph J. | last2=Witten | first2=Edward | title=The Hagedorn transition and the number of degrees of freedom of string theory | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=310 | issue=2 | year=1988 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90151-4 | pages=291–334| bibcode=1988NuPhB.310..291A }}</ref> or 
[[quantum field theory]].<ref name="auto">{{cite journal | last1=Lauscher | first1=Oliver | last2=Reuter | first2=Martin | title=Fractal spacetime structure in asymptotically safe gravity | journal=Journal of High Energy Physics | volume=2005 | issue=10 | date=2005-10-18 | issn=1029-8479 | doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2005/10/050 | page=050| arxiv=hep-th/0508202 | bibcode=2005JHEP...10..050L | s2cid=14396108 }}</ref>

==Examples==
The diffusion of ink in an [[isotropic]] homogeneous medium like still water evolves as <math>t^{3/2}</math>, giving a spectral dimension of 3. 

Ink in a 2D [[Sierpiński triangle]] diffuses following a more complicated path and thus more slowly, as <math>t^{0.6826}</math>, giving a spectral dimension of 1.3652.<ref name="Sierpinski fractals">[https://www2.icp.uni-stuttgart.de/~hilfer/publications/renormalisation-on-sierpinski-type-fractals-Hilfer.pdf R. Hilfer and A. Blumen (1984) "Renormalisation on Sierpinski-type fractals"] J. Phys. A: Math. Gen. 17 </ref>
